cluster: Bulk-flow measurement lineage (CF4 minimum-variance + mock calibration)

prior_art.reference: Watkins, Feldman & Hudson 2009, MNRAS 392, 743, 'Consistently large cosmic flows on scales of 100 h^-1 Mpc: a challenge for the standard LCDM cosmology' (arXiv:0809.4041)
prior_art.what_it_did: Introduced the minimum-variance (MV) bulk-flow estimator: weights chosen to minimize the variance between the survey moment and the moment an 'ideal' Gaussian-window survey of a given scale would measure, using an analytic linear-theory velocity covariance/power spectrum. This is the exact 'MV ideal-window' machinery our result re-implements.
prior_art.overlap: Our 'MV ideal-window' estimator IS this method. The ideal-window-tied-to-scale-R construction, the Lagrange-multiplier weights, and the analytic linear-theory covariance we compare against are all defined here. Direct methodological ancestor; currently mis-cited in our bib.

prior_art.reference: Agarwal, Feldman & Watkins 2012, MNRAS 424, 2667, 'Testing the minimum variance method for estimating large-scale velocity moments' (arXiv:1204.4839)
prior_art.what_it_did: Validated the MV estimator by extracting mock catalogues from N-body simulations (LasDamas, Horizon Run) and passing them through the MV weights, comparing MV-weighted moments to Gaussian-weighted box moments. Concluded the MV estimators are unbiased and 'negligibly affected by non-linear flows.'
prior_art.overlap: Establishes that passing mocks through the MV weights to validate the estimator and its covariance is >13-year-old standard practice, not a new technique. Our 'in-house forward mock through the identical MV estimator' is exactly this validation loop.

prior_art.reference: Peery, Watkins & Feldman 2018, MNRAS 481, 1368, 'Easily interpretable bulk flows: continuing tension with the standard cosmological model' (arXiv:1808.07772)
prior_art.what_it_did: Refined the MV method to give a scale-R interpretable bulk flow with an added constraint making the estimate independent of H0; applied to CosmicFlows-3, found tension at 150 h^-1 Mpc. The 'Peery MVE' is the ideal-window-at-scale-R variant.
prior_art.overlap: The specific 'ideal-window tied to a Gaussian scale R' flavor our card describes (Gaussian window scale, uniform-flow-exact constraint) matches the Peery variant, not just the 2009 base. Should be cited as the direct estimator we run.

prior_art.reference: Watkins, Allen, Bradford et al. 2023, MNRAS 524, 1885, 'Analysing the large-scale bulk flow using cosmicflows4: increasing tension with the standard cosmological model' (arXiv:2302.02028)
prior_art.what_it_did: Ran the MV estimator on CF4. Reported |B|(200 h^-1 Mpc) = 419 +/- 36 km/s toward l=298+/-5, b=-8+/-4; tension probabilities ~0.015% at 150 h^-1 Mpc and ~1.5e-4% (>4 sigma) at 200 h^-1 Mpc, assessed against the analytic linear-theory covariance.
prior_art.overlap: This is the direct prior for our headline |B|(200)=405 km/s and our 4.4-5.4 sigma tension range. Our amplitude is consistent within errors (<0.4 sigma of 419+/-36) and our tension magnitude and direction reproduce theirs. Our result is a re-measurement of theirs on CF4 groups.

prior_art.reference: Whitford, Howlett & Davis 2023, MNRAS 526, 3051, 'Evaluating bulk flow estimators for CosmicFlows-4 measurements' (arXiv:2306.11269)
prior_art.what_it_did: Tested four estimators (Kaiser MLE, Nusser MLE, Watkins MVE, Peery MVE) against CF4 using three mock families passed through the estimator weights: (1) 'simplistic' Gaussian-random-field mocks drawn from the linear-theory covariance, (2) L-PICOLA Zeldovich/linear-only mocks, (3) L-PICOLA full non-linear mocks (Qin 2019/2021, Howlett 2022). Found the estimator uncertainties are typically UNDERESTIMATED -> tension with LCDM is OVERESTIMATED, and small biases toward underestimated |B| arise from non-linear peculiar velocities. MVE gave 428+/-108 km/s at 173 h^-1 Mpc (0.11% probability).
prior_art.overlap: This is the direct prior for essentially our entire mock-calibration contribution: GRF-through-MVE, linear-vs-nonlinear split, the 'variance underestimated / tension overestimated' framing, and the localization of the significance reduction to non-linear power are all Whitford's central results. Our conclusion IS Whitford's conclusion.

prior_art.reference: Watkins & Feldman 2026, arXiv:2512.03168, 'The Origins of the Bulk flow'
prior_art.what_it_did: Decomposed the CF4 MV bulk flow into internal (mass within 200 h^-1 Mpc) and external (beyond 200 h^-1 Mpc) contributions; found the large-scale flow is dominated by sources beyond 200 h^-1 Mpc whose amplitude grows monotonically with scale, and challenged the assumption that the externally-driven flow is spatially uniform. beta=0.31+/-0.01, H0=75.0.
prior_art.overlap: This is the direct prior for our 'super-sample (>box) uniform bulk mode' ingredient. The super-survey/external-mode contribution to bulk flow is a published, actively-studied physical effect, so adding a uniform super-box mode to a GRF box is not a novel modeling insight. Note Watkins & Feldman actively dispute the 'uniform' approximation our mock adopts.

prior_art.reference: Boubel, Howlett, Said et al. 2024 (CosmicFlows-4 Tully-Fisher forward model of the first spherical velocity modes / H0)
prior_art.what_it_did: Bayesian forward model of the first two spherical modes of the velocity field (monopole/radial + dipole/bulk flow) with minimal LCDM assumptions, applied to the CF4 Tully-Fisher sample, also delivering an H0 estimate. A prior-free measurement approach that treats the data directly rather than via an intermediate distance estimator.
prior_art.overlap: Adjacent, not overlapping: a different (forward-model, not MV ideal-window) route to the CF4 bulk flow. Relevant as a contemporaneous alternative that does NOT report the >4 sigma tension in the same terms; worth citing as method context but does not pre-empt our specific MV numbers.

prior_art.reference: Boubel-Rubin-Do et al. (Hawai'i Supernova Flows) 2026, arXiv:2606.17142, 'Hawai`i Supernova Flows: Bulk Flow Measurements using SNe Ia in the Optical and NIR'
prior_art.what_it_did: Independent-tracer bulk-flow measurement using >400 SNe Ia (optical + NIR), two bulk-flow estimators, two distance estimators, out to z<~0.1. Inferred speeds ~100-400 km/s, all CONSISTENT with LCDM.
prior_art.overlap: Counterpoint prior art: an independent 2026 dataset finds NO significant LCDM tension in the bulk flow, reinforcing that the CF4 >4 sigma signal is likely tracer/covariance-driven (the 'likely over-estimate' our result flags). Should be cited so our caveat is grounded in current literature, not just asserted.

per_result_verdicts.reason: Reproduces Watkins et al. 2023 (419+/-36 km/s at 200 h^-1 Mpc) within <0.4 sigma using the same estimator on the same catalogue. A faithful re-measurement, not a new value. The apex direction likewise matches. Legitimate as a validation but carries no amplitude novelty.

per_result_verdicts.reason: Watkins 2023 already reported the CF4 tension as >4 sigma (1.5e-4% probability) using the analytic covariance, and Whitford 2023 already showed that this analytic-covariance significance is over-estimated because the covariance is underestimated. per_result_verdicts.reason: Passing mocks through MV weights is standard since Agarwal-Feldman-Watkins 2012; GRF mocks drawn from the linear-theory covariance passed through the MVE are Whitford 2023's 'simplistic mocks'; the super-sample external mode is the subject of Watkins & Feldman 2026. per_result_verdicts.reason: Linear-mock-vs-linear-analytic agreement near unity is expected by construction and confirms only that the estimator/geometry/noise do not inflate the variance -- precisely Whitford 2023's finding that the MVE is unbiased and its analytic covariance tracks the linear mocks. per_result_verdicts.result: Localizing the literature 2-3 sigma reduction (from ~5.8 sigma) to non-linear power
per_result_verdicts.reason: Whitford 2023 demonstrated exactly this with L-PICOLA linear (Zeldovich) vs full non-linear mocks, attributing the variance underestimation and the tension reduction to non-linear peculiar velocities. Critically, our own card (rev-r197) states the non-linear/COLA mock is NOT run and is a downgraded residual -- so we cite the reduction rather than independently demonstrate it. This is re-attribution to Whitford, not new evidence.

per_result_verdicts.reason: The end-to-end pipeline (MV ideal-window estimator + mocks through the weights + linear-vs-nonlinear covariance calibration) is the Watkins-2009 / Agarwal-2012 / Peery-2018 / Watkins-2023 / Whitford-2023 program reproduced in-house. Value is in independent code verification and integration into the Bianchi/HTT comparator, not in method or physics novelty.

novelty_statement: On the external-literature axis this cluster is a faithful reproduction of an already-mature program, and the manuscript should say so plainly. The MV ideal-window estimator (Watkins-Feldman-Hudson 2009; Peery-Watkins-Feldman 2018), the practice of passing mocks through the MV weights to calibrate its covariance (Agarwal-Feldman-Watkins 2012), the specific CF4 measurement of |B|(200)~419 km/s at >4 sigma (Watkins et al. 2023), the demonstration that this analytic-covariance significance is over-estimated and that the reduction to ~2-3 sigma is driven by non-linear peculiar velocities (Whitford-Howlett-Davis 2023, using both GRF and L-PICOLA linear/non-linear mocks through the same estimators), and even the super-sample/external-mode origin of the flow (Watkins-Feldman 2026) are all published. Our |B|(200)=405 km/s reproduces Watkins 2023 within 0.4 sigma; our GRF+super-sample forward mock reproduces Whitford's 'simplistic' GRF-through-MVE branch; our headline that the estimator/geometry do not inflate and the true reduction is non-linear is Whitford's central conclusion -- and, honestly, we cite that reduction rather than reproduce it, since our own card records that the non-linear/COLA mock is not run. The only genuinely in-house elements are the independent implementation and the embedding of this pipeline into the Bianchi/HTT comparator; none of it is a NEW physical or methodological result. Recommended framing: present this as an independent reproduction and cross-check of the CF4 bulk-flow tension literature (CONFIRMATORY), not as a new significance methodology, and add the missing lineage citations below. A referee will otherwise flag the absence of Watkins-2009, Agarwal-2012, Peery-2018 and (fatally) the mis-attributed Watkins-2023 entry.

novelty_statement: This CF4 fsigma8 measurement is, honestly, a confirmatory reproduction rather than a new result. The estimator described — a field-level Gaussian maximum-likelihood fit of the velocity covariance with a single linear amplitude, C(A)=A·G+N, evaluated in a whitened eigenbasis — is the Jaffe-Kaiser (1995) / Johnson et al. (2014) velocity-power-spectrum method, identical in structure to the DESI 'maximum likelihood fields method' (Lai & Howlett 2026) and the generalized framework of Ravoux et al. (2025); the whitening step is the standard signal-to-noise / Karhunen-Loeve eigenmode transform (Tegmark, Taylor & Heavens 1997), and octant jackknife errors are routine. The recovered value fsigma8 = 0.40 falls inside the tight low-redshift consensus (0.34-0.42) and is essentially indistinguishable from Boruah, Hudson & Lavaux (2020, 0.400+/-0.017); CF4 itself has already been analysed for the growth rate by Courtois et al. (2023, grouped-CF4 0.36+/-0.05), Boubel et al. (2024, TF 0.35+/-0.03) and Wang/Feldman/Watkins/Yang (2026, 0.384). The single defensible novelty is the specific pairing of the Johnson-2014-style ML velocity-COVARIANCE estimator with the full CF4 GROUP catalogue (previous CF4 growth-rate work used correlation functions or TF forward-modelling), which is at most an incremental extension. per_result_verdicts.reason: I found NO published DESI (DR1 or later) galaxy number-count / Ellis-Baldwin kinematic dipole. Existing DESI dipole work is different observables: the relativistic galaxy-cross-correlation dipole (Bonvin-style, e.g. MNRAS 525, 4611; ELG-LRG 13-21 sigma) and Doppler-magnification-dipole forecasts (arXiv:2511.17858), plus the DR1 PV growth-rate survey. So the raw number D on DESI BGS is not in the literature. But it is a straightforward application of the established Ellis-Baldwin/number-count estimator to a new dataset, is explicitly diagnostic-only, and (as a partial-sky, z<0.1 spectroscopic sample) is not a clean cosmological dipole — hence incremental, not new physics or new method.

per_result_verdicts.result: The BGS number-count dipole is clustering-dominated (13.5 sigma above shot noise) and NOT a kinematic probe at BGS depth
per_result_verdicts.reason: Established for over a decade: Gibelyou & Huterer 2012 (local-structure dipole A~0.1 at z_max~0.1 >> kinematic ~0.003), Yoon & Huterer 2015 (local-structure dipole dominates ell=1 in all extant LSS surveys; deep + wide-sky + ~30M galaxies needed to detect kinematics), Tiwari et al. 2024 and Peebles 2022. A low-z, fsky~0.28 sample being clustering-dominated is the textbook expectation, not a finding.

per_result_verdicts.result: The measured dipole is consistent with LambdaCDM clustering cosmic variance (mock |D|=0.021+-0.009, p=0.90) — NOT an excess
per_result_verdicts.reason: Reproduces the known LambdaCDM prediction that low-z number-count dipoles are dominated by (and consistent with) clustering cosmic variance: Yoo, Magi & Huterer 2025 and 'Addressing Dipole Tension via Clustering' (arXiv:2508.18259) both show LambdaCDM clustering supplies a large low-z dipole. Producing p=0.90 via an in-house mock is a legitimate but confirmatory reproduction of an established conclusion on a new dataset.

per_result_verdicts.result: Exact ell=1-projection GRF mock calibration (observed dN/dz -> GRF sky maps, masked to BGS footprint + Poisson, identical estimator, 400 mocks x 3 bias) for the masked dipole significance
per_result_verdicts.reason: Mock/GRF-with-survey-mask + Poisson null calibration of a masked number-count dipole is the standard significance methodology (Secrest et al. 2022; Wagenveld et al. 2023-2025; Gibelyou & Huterer 2012 clustering-dipole variance; Yoon & Huterer 2015). The exact-ell=1 projection of the observed dN/dz into a clustering GRF is a sound and conventional implementation, not a new technique. No novelty claim for the method is defensible.

per_result_verdicts.result: Kinematic component sub-dominant at BGS depth
per_result_verdicts.reason: Directly follows from Ellis & Baldwin 1984 (kinematic amplitude ~[2+x(1+alpha)]v/c ~ few e-3) versus the local-structure dipole (~0.1) established by Gibelyou & Huterer 2012 and Yoon & Huterer 2015; Wagenveld et al. 2025 make the kinematic-vs-non-kinematic split explicit. novelty_statement: Referee assessment: The one genuinely fresh element is the dataset — I could find no published DESI (DR1 or later) galaxy number-count / Ellis-Baldwin kinematic dipole; the only DESI 'dipole' literature concerns the relativistic galaxy-cross-correlation dipole and Doppler-magnification forecasts, which are different observables. So the number D = 9.49e-3 for DESI BGS is not previously in print. However, the scientific content is not new. That a low-redshift (z<0.1), partial-sky (fsky~0.28) galaxy sample yields a number-count dipole dominated by local clustering rather than the kinematic v/c signal, and that this is fully consistent with LambdaCDM once clustering cosmic variance is included, is established prior art (Gibelyou & Huterer 2012; Yoon & Huterer 2015; Tiwari et al. 2024; Yoo, Magi & Huterer 2025; 'Addressing Dipole Tension via Clustering' 2026). The exact-ell=1-projection GRF-with-mask + Poisson mock calibration is the standard significance methodology (Secrest et al. 2022; Wagenveld et al. 2023-2025), not a new estimator. The correct classification is therefore an incremental dataset extension delivering a confirmatory reproduction of an already-known result. The authors' own framing — 'clustering-dominated, consistent with LambdaCDM, NOT an excess, diagnostic-only' — is exactly right and matches the literature; the manuscript should present it as such and must not imply that finding a null/consistent low-z dipole is itself notable. The main referee requirement is proper crediting: the paper currently risks 'missing citation' flags because the entire clustering-domination-at-low-z result and the Ellis-Baldwin estimator are pre-existing. Any added value would have to come from DESI-specific systematics control or a redshift-dipole (clustering-insensitive) kinematic extraction in the Tiwari et al. 2024 vein, neither of which the number-count measurement provides.

per_result_verdicts.result: (a-i)
per_result_verdicts.reason: A linear Wiener-filter velocity reconstruction is irrotational by construction: the estimator derives v from the gradient of a reconstructed potential (Zaroubi, Hoffman & Dekel 1999; Fisher et al. 1995). Measuring curl/div ~ 0.009 confirms the estimator is behaving as designed — a self-consistency/sanity check, not a physical measurement of the vorticity of the true field. It borders on ALREADY_KNOWN; it is confirmatory because the specific numerical residual on CF4++ had not been tabulated, but no new physics is established. It should NOT be phrased as a physical 'potential-flow' or 'no-go' result about the Universe, because AI reconstructions (arXiv:2604.14653) and N-body (arXiv:2506.15486) show real vorticity exists on nonlinear scales.

per_result_verdicts.result: (a-ii)
per_result_verdicts.reason: The Hoffman-Ribak constrained-realization residual is a standard GRF that restores WF-suppressed power and necessarily carries a rotational (curl) component (Hoffman & Ribak 1991; Lilow & Nusser 2021 CORAS). That the residual vorticity is residual-dominated and correlation-length-dependent is expected behavior of the method, and our own card labels it PARTIAL / BLOCKED_MISSING_FIELD_REALIZATIONS. No novel claim; reproduces known CR phenomenology.

Multi-method velocity-field / bulk-flow reconstruction comparison is an established genre: the Velocity Field Olympics (Stiskalek et al. 2025) benchmarks six reconstructions; Lilow et al. 2024 compares NN vs CORAS; Whitford et al. 2023 compares CF4 estimators; Courtois 2023 / Valade 2024 add HMC and forward modeling. Our specific column assemblage (CF4 PV variants + CF4++ WF + Carrick + LVN + CORAS) is a new particular combination, and the qualitative conclusion — reconstruction/method-driven spread with amplitudes broadly agreeing within ~1-2 sigma and 2MRS reconstructions regressing to the mean at large r — reproduces the published consensus. Legitimate as a diagnostic cross-check, but conceptually incremental, not new.

novelty_statement: Neither headline in this cluster is novel as a physics result, and the manuscript's own diagnostic-only framing is the correct one. Result (a) — that the Wiener-filter mean field on CF4++ has curl/div ~ 0.009 — is a tautology of the estimator: linear WF and constrained-realization reconstructions build the velocity as the gradient of a potential (Zaroubi, Hoffman & Dekel 1999; Fisher et al. 1995), so they are irrotational by construction and the near-zero curl is a self-consistency check, not a measurement of the true field's vorticity. Crucially, the true nonlinear velocity field is NOT irrotational (N-body vorticity power spectra, arXiv:2506.15486; AI vorticity reconstructions of SDSS/local-universe data, arXiv:2604.14653), so any language suggesting a 'potential-flow no-go' about the Universe would be an overclaim; the honest statement is 'the linear WF field is curl-free by construction, as expected.' The CR vorticity band is likewise standard Hoffman-Ribak residual behavior. Result (b), the 7-method reconstruction-dependence table, sits squarely inside an active, crowded genre (the Velocity Field Olympics of Stiskalek et al. 2025 benchmarks six methods; Whitford et al. 2023 benchmarks CF4 estimators; Lilow et al. 2024 already publishes an NN-vs-CORAS bulk-flow comparison), and its conclusion — method-driven amplitude spread with cross-method agreement at the 1-2 sigma level and 2MRS reconstructions regressing to the mean at large radius — reproduces the established consensus that bulk-flow amplitude/direction is estimator- and geometry-dependent. As a referee I would accept both as supporting diagnostics/robustness checks (CONFIRMATORY and INCREMENTAL respectively) provided the manuscript cites the by-construction irrotationality literature and the existing multi-method comparisons, and drops any implication that the curl test is a novel physical anomaly or no-go.

per_result_verdicts.result: Rank-2 identifiability of the comparator with structural null {W^2, Omega_k}
per_result_verdicts.reason: That anisotropy sectors are mutually degenerate / not independently constrainable from the CMB is already recognized (Pontzen 2009 'full freedom of the Bianchi CMB anomalies'; general CMB parameter-degeneracy literature). Casting it as a formal rank-2 identifiability statement with an explicit structural-null pair is a genuine new formalization, but it sharpens a known degeneracy rather than discovering an unknown one. No external source found stating the exact {W^2, Omega_k} structural null, so the specific claim is unverified externally (borderline NEW), but the phenomenon is known.

novelty_statement: The physics content of this cluster is, for the most part, a careful re-organization and reproduction of a well-established literature rather than new results. The master departure identity is a signed re-packaging of the standard expansion-normalized (orthonormal-frame) constraint equation of Bianchi cosmology (Wainwright-Ellis 1997; Ellis-Maartens-MacCallum 2012), and the sector bounds it books are those of the Barrow-Juszkiewicz-Sonoda (1985) -> Kogut (1997) -> MES (1995) -> Pontzen-Challinor (2007) -> McEwen (2013) -> Saadeh (2016) -> Planck-2018 lineage; the 'MES modernization' is an honest reproduction-plus-correction of Maartens-Ellis-Stoeger, and the King-Ellis rotating-congruence results extend a mature tilted-Bianchi dynamical-systems program. The one element that appears genuinely new is methodological, not physical: I could find no prior use of econometrics-style partial identification (interval identified sets, Imbens-Manski 2004 confidence intervals) applied to CMB or peculiar-velocity anisotropy sectors, and the closely related rank-2 identifiability / structural-null formalization sharpens a degeneracy that the community has only discussed informally (Pontzen 2009). My recommendation is that the paper foreground the partial-identification transfer and the identifiability formalization as its actual contribution, explicitly cite the econometric provenance (Imbens-Manski, Manski, Molinari) so the method is not mistaken for internal invention, and frame the identity, MES bounds and tilted-congruence dynamics as consolidation/reproduction of prior work with proper attribution — otherwise a referee will read the physics sections as restating known results. It must also engage the near-contemporaneous tilted-dipole papers (Krishnan-Mondol-Sheikh-Jabbari 2023; Martin-Skordis et al. 2025) to establish that its observational scope is distinct.
